That said… wow, it was crazy crowded when I went 😅. The boats on the lake weren’t running either, which was a bit of a bummer. Imagine a massive park with a huge lake in the middle, surrounded by temples, bridges, and these beautiful old pavilions that look like they’re straight out of a kung fu movie. It’s peaceful, green, and full of history. One of the coolest things is how the whole place is designed around the themes of longevity and harmony. The main hill is literally called Longevity Hill, and the lake – Kunming Lake – was man-made to symbolize the sea, with the palace representing a mythical island of immortality. Even the decorations, like the cranes and pine trees, are symbols of long life and good fortune. It’s like the whole place is whispering, “Take it easy, live long, be kind.” The Summer Palace was basically the playground of Empress Dowager Cixi, also known as the Dragon Lady. She was one of the most powerful women in Chinese history, ruled from behind the scenes for decades during the late Qing Dynasty. There’s even this long corridor – the Long Gallery – that stretches forever (okay, it’s like 728 meters, but still). It’s covered in thousands of paintings, and rumor has it Cixi used to stroll there to enjoy the lake breeze and keep an eye on things. She even used funds meant for the navy to renovate the palac. All in all, the Summer Palace is a must-see. It’s like a mix of nature, art, and drama – with a bit of imperial gossip thrown in. Just wear comfy shoes. It’s huge.

Summer Palace 頣和园 yiheyuan Beijing is a UNESCO world heritage site built around Longevity Hill and Kuming Lake. The Longevity hill 60 metres (200 ft) high have steep rocks as steps and might be strenuous for some others to climb up.( ✌︎'ω')✌︎ Summer Palace is a place of retreat for the Qing Dynasty Royal family. Once up the Longevity Hill, you will see the Tower of Fragrance of Buddha, Hall of Benevolence and Longevity, the massive man-made Kunming lake where the excavated soil was used to built the Longevity Hill. A must visit scenic spot in Beijing for its history, culture and breathtaking scenery.

颐和园 or Summer Palace was a built by Emperor Qianlong to celebrate his mother's birthday in 1750. It was later used as vacation venue by emperors and empresses. Really tranquil to visit and walk about before the crowd starts to arrive which could be as early as 06:30am. Enjoyed the part starting from the Wenchang Tower, near to the Heralding Spring Pavilion facing the Kunming Lake before the Long Corridor, which you could see the Tower of Fragrance of Buddha and the Seventeen-arch Bridge. Along the 728m Long Corridor, do look up at the ceiling and enjoy the painted murals. Indeed a very wonderful imperial garden. If have extra time, may wish to visit the museum situated within the Wenchang Gallery.

It depends which entrance you use, but I’d really recommend checking the side with the Marble Boat—it’s one of the highlights here. From there you can hop on a boat across the lake (about 40 yuan), which is very scenic and gives you a great view of the palace grounds. The little souvenir shop opposite the Marble Boat also has surprisingly good quality items. I was here about 15 years ago and it definitely has improved since then—more organized, easier to get around, and still just as beautiful. Overall, I had a really positive experience. From the moment I stepped into Summer Palace at the China World Summit Wing, I knew I was in for an extraordinary dining experience. This isn't just a meal; it’s a sublime journey into the heart of authentic, elevated Chinese cuisine. The ambiance is a masterclass in understated luxury elegant, serene, and tastefully decorated with traditional Chinese art, creating an atmosphere that is both grand and intimate. It’s the perfect setting for a special occasion or an impressive business dinner. The true star, however, is the food. Each dish is a testament to the artistry and skill of the culinary team. We began with the signature Peking Duck, and it was, without exaggeration, the best I have ever tasted. The skin was an impossibly crisp, caramelized perfection, and the meat was succulent and flavorful, served with delicate pancakes and all the traditional accompaniments. The Wok-fried Lobster with Ginger and Spring Onion was another highlight—incredibly fresh, expertly cooked, and bursting with clean, aromatic flavors. Every ingredient sang with quality and freshness. Service deserves its own accolades. The staff is the epitome of polished, attentive professionalism. Our server was exceptionally knowledgeable, guiding us through the extensive menu with genuine passion and offering perfect wine pairings. Their attention to detail—from timely course changes to anticipating our needs—was flawless and made us feel genuinely valued. In a city teeming with dining options, Summer Palace stands in a league of its own. It successfully marries time-honored Cantonese traditions with contemporary finesse, resulting in an unforgettable gastronomic event. It is, without a doubt, worth every penny and more. For anyone seeking the pinnacle of Chinese fine dining in Beijing, look no further. This is a flawless, five-star experience that I will dream about until my next visit. Highly, highly recommended.

We visited Yiheyuan (the Summer Palace) about 30 minutes before sunset, and unfortunately, it turned out to be the wrong timing. As closing time approached, many visitors were rushing to exit the park, which created a sense of pressure and made the experience feel hurried rather than relaxing. Instead of enjoying the scenery at our own pace, we found ourselves constantly moving with the crowd. As daylight faded, visibility dropped quickly, and many parts of the palace grounds became harder to appreciate. The lake, corridors, and architectural details that Yiheyuan is famous for are best enjoyed in daylight, and once it got dark, there really wasn’t much left to see. Some areas also felt quieter and less atmospheric than expected, possibly due to the season and the time of day. While Yiheyuan is undeniably beautiful and historically significant, this visit highlighted how important timing is. I would strongly recommend coming earlier in the day, ideally in the morning or early afternoon, to fully enjoy the vast gardens, lakeside views, and detailed architecture without feeling rushed. A beautiful place — just make sure to plan your visit wisely.

The Summer Palace is a vast ensemble of lakes, gardens, and imperial palaces in Beijing, China, and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is widely regarded as a masterpiece of classical Chinese landscape garden design, seamlessly integrating natural hills and water with man-made features like pavilions, halls, and bridges. Original Construction: The palace was first commissioned in 1750 during the Qing Dynasty by the Qianlong Emperor as a gift for his mother and was originally named the "Garden of Clear Ripples" (Qingyiyuan). Destruction and Reconstruction: It was destroyed by Anglo-French forces during the Second Opium War in 1860. It was later lavishly reconstructed and renamed the Summer Palace (Yíhéyuán) starting in 1888 by Empress Dowager Cixi, who used it as her summer residence and a place to handle state affairs. Later Years: The palace was damaged again during the Boxer Rebellion in 1900 but was restored. Following the end of the Qing Dynasty in 1912, it eventually became a public park in 1924.

Finding a quiet corner to soak in the natural beauty and historical charm can be a challenge, but it’s worth the effort. One highly recommended experience is renting an electric boat. Gliding across the lake offers a peaceful escape from the crowds and gives you a unique perspective of the palace, its bridges, and the surrounding scenery. The Summer Palace, a vast complex of palaces, Chinese landscape gardens, and lakes, was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1998. We took tram line 4 and entered via the Northern gate. We immediately climbed the Longevity Hill, which was probably a mistake. While the view was breathtaking, there was nothing much to see apart from the colourful Tibetan-style architecture and decorations. We couldn't explore the inside of any of the buildings. We were, by then, too tired to fully explore the lake and garden area.

The Summer Palace in Beijing is a true masterpiece of Chinese imperial landscape art. The buildings, palaces, and pavilions blend into a panorama of hills, gardens, and water, evoking a living painting. After the original palace was looted and destroyed by British and French troops during the Opium Wars (see Victor Hugo's excellent letter to Captain Bulter on this subject), the palace was rebuilt to restore the site to its former splendor and tranquility. You can take advantage of your morning excursion on the Great Wall to visit the Summer Palace in the afternoon. Even if the crowds are large, the size of the site allows for large numbers of visitors without spoiling everyone's experience. If you are there at the end of the day, buy a ticket to sail on Kunming Lake aboard one of the boats. A guaranteed spectacle

A stunning UNESCO World Heritage Site that reflects the grandeur of China, this location spans vast grounds featuring picturesque lakes, traditional pavilions, and intricately designed bridges. It offers a serene retreat from the bustling city. The views from Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake are breathtaking, especially during sunrise or sunset. Strolling through the elaborately crafted pathways and exploring iconic landmarks like the Marble Boat and the Seventeen-Arch Bridge feels like stepping back in time. It’s a must-visit destination for anyone seeking to experience history, culture, and natural beauty in Beijing.

The Summer Palace is an expansive and stunning destination, so be sure to allocate at least 3 to 4 hours to fully explore this incredible site. We reached the palace easily by subway, getting off at Beigongmen Station. Entering from the north side, we were immediately captivated by the charming Suzhou Street and the serene Suzhou River, which set the tone for the rest of the visit. Our journey continued with a climb up many steps to the magnificent Tower of Buddhist Incense, offering breathtaking views of the surrounding area. From there, we wandered down to the famous Long Corridor, marveling at its intricate artwork and details. One of the highlights was the ferry tour on Kunming Lake, which provided a unique perspective of the palace grounds. The ferry even stops at the iconic Marco Polo Bridge, a picturesque spot that’s worth exploring. For our final adventure, we climbed to the top of the Tower of Incense, where we were rewarded with an incredible panoramic view of Kunming Lake and the surrounding landscape. The Summer Palace is truly a masterpiece of natural beauty and cultural heritage. Whether you’re soaking in the scenery, admiring the historical architecture, or simply enjoying the tranquil atmosphere, this place is a must-visit when in Beijing.

The rich history and intricate architecture make it a must-see. Despite the summer crowds, the expansive grounds provide plenty of space to explore and find peaceful spots. The Long Corridor, with its detailed paintings, and the Marble Boat are highlights. Renting a boat on Kunming Lake offers a unique perspective of the palace. The grounds are well-maintained, and the entry fee is fair given the vastness and beauty of the site. Highly recommend bringing water and comfortable shoes for a full day of exploring this historical gem. Don't miss this enchanting escape in Beijing!
Very beautiful place. Worth to take boat and also a guide to tell you story of the place.

The Summer Palace is a tranquil escape from Beijing's bustling city life, showcasing exquisite gardens, pavilions, and the stunning Kunming Lake. Its harmonious blend of natural beauty and man-made structures is unparalleled. Don’t miss the Long Corridor and a boat ride on the lake for serene views. That made my visit a bit uncomfortable as they were thousands and thousands of people all around. Architecture of the Summer Palace is amazing and it is full of history. I used East and South-East entrance. Even in public holiday and nice weather, I didn’t have to wait more than 10 minutes to get tickets, which are affordable and worth the expense. There are nice paths and bridges to walk in quiet; also the lake is beautiful. I strongly suggest to pay the integrated ticket that allows you to see all attractions inside, as the Hall of the See of Wisdom and its Thousand-Hand Buddha Statue are amazing!!!

If you are a foreigner, expect people wanting to take picture with you - we had 4 different people approach us for a photo during the visit. Nestled in the heart of Beijing, the Summer Palace stands as a testament to China's rich history and architectural splendor. This UNESCO World Heritage Site offers a serene retreat from the bustling city, inviting visitors to immerse themselves in a world of natural beauty and cultural significance. The Summer Palace is a picturesque landscape of tranquility and elegance. Its vast gardens, serene Kunming Lake, intricately designed pavilions, and ancient bridges create a mesmerizing panorama. Whether strolling along the Long Corridor adorned with vibrant paintings or admiring the views from the Marble Boat, every corner exudes a sense of timeless beauty. The Summer Palace is an enchanting haven that seamlessly intertwines natural beauty with historical grandeur. It's a place where one can appreciate the splendor of ancient China while finding solace amidst its breathtaking surroundings. A visit here is not just a sightseeing excursion but a profound journey through time and culture.

This Is A Spectacular Summer Palace The Place Is Huge, I recommend To Give Yourself At Least Half A Day Here. Beautiful Architecture And Amazing Scenery. It's A Good 15mins Walk From The Metro Station.

From there, it’s a short walk to the ticket booth. The entrance fee is 20 RMB per person. If you enjoy photography and exploring the beautiful scenery, make sure to allocate at least 4 hours for your visit.

We enjoyed taking photos, walking and of course enjoying the snacks of sausages and drinks while inside this historical site.

If you are visiting Beijing, this is a must see sightseeing spot. Depending from what gate you enter, be ready to walk up and down some stairs. To have the best view of the palace without going on a boat, go from the north to the east side of the see. Book Tickets one day in advance (the best for that is Trip.com) and try to go on a sunny day for the best views). We spend around 3 hours here.

Apart from visiting the Forbidden Palace, this place is definitely worth a visit when in Beijing. It’s the Chinese imperial family’s vacation location and the size of this place is just…jaw-dropping. A beautiful lake, even more scenic during the winter season as you can skate on the frozen lake. Lots and lots of temples and spots to visit!

Lovely palace on the edge of Beijing. Easy to reach on the metro. Quite hilly and steep in parts but rewarded by delightful views over Kunming Lake. Worth paying the extra ¥15 to enter the enormous lakeside Buddhist temple and pagoda The Tower of Buddhist Incense. Also the 700m Long Corridor which runs adjacent to the lake is a real feature. Our family visit to the Summer Palace in September 2025 was a good experience, rich with history and beauty. It is undoubtedly good for learning; walking through the grounds brings China’s imperial past to life. We admired the intricate details of the Long Corridor’s paintings, learned about Empress Dowager Cixi on the Marble Boat, and enjoyed the serene views over Kunming Lake. A fair warning: you have to walk a lot. The complex is vast, and exploring the key sites involves considerable distances. This made it somewhat tiring for our kids, so we took frequent breaks by the lake and enjoyed a short boat ride, which was a welcome respite. Despite the tired little legs, the stunning landscapes, historic pavilions, and the sense of stepping into another era made it all worthwhile. The late-summer weather was pleasant, and the crowds were manageable. Overall, I recommend the Summer Palace for families. Just go prepared with comfortable shoes, snacks, and a plan that includes relaxing boat trips to balance the extensive walking. It’s a memorable and educational day out.

The Summer Palace in Beijing is a captivating blend of imperial grandeur and natural beauty. Nestled on the shores of Kunming Lake, this UNESCO World Heritage site is a testament to China's rich history. The sprawling complex boasts a harmonious combination of classical architecture, lush gardens, and serene waterscapes. Walking through the intricately designed corridors, one can sense the opulence that once graced the Qing Dynasty. The Hall of Benevolence and Longevity, with its vibrant colors and intricate details, reflects the cultural richness of Chinese craftsmanship. The Long Corridor, adorned with thousands of paintings, offers a leisurely stroll with picturesque views of the lake. Kunming Lake, with its graceful bridges and iconic Marble Boat, adds a tranquil touch to the palace's allure. Boating on the lake during the warmer months provides a unique perspective of the surrounding structures. While the Summer Palace is a haven of aesthetic delights, it also serves as a historical treasure trove. Visitors can explore the various halls, pavilions, and temples, each holding stories of bygone eras. In summary, the Summer Palace is a masterpiece that seamlessly integrates art, nature, and history. Its enchanting ambiance and cultural significance make it a must-visit destination for those seeking a glimpse into China's imperial past.

This UNESCO site is probably the most enchanting place I've visited in China. It exudes an old imperial beauty, that takes you on an immersive journey back to the splendour of the Qing Dynasty. It covers an area of approximately 3 sq kms, so be prepared for a trek while taking in the visual delights of attractions such as The Hall of Longevity, The Marble Boat, The Long Corridor, The 17 Arch Bridge, The Dragon Temple, and a collection of lakes, vast gardens, pavilions, temples, all with many tales from a medieval era. This picturesque area is located on the outskirts of Western Beijing. We came here on a lovely June day for a half day tour after visiting the Great Wall, and so we were able to see the natural beauty of the Chinese countryside along the way, complete with quaint villages and locals all out picking a huge range of fruit from the plenty of orchards we saw. The Summer Palace grounds was pretty crowded with locals at the time we went (after 2pm), but that didn't take away from this amazing experience. We took a serene boating trip around Kunming Lake on an old school traditional Chinese boat, to get a different view of the Summer Palace and other landmarks in the area. This definitely saves you a lot of walking in the heat and is worth the trip. Incidentally, Kunming Lake is artificially made, with all the water taken and transported from the Yangtze River in the South of the country, which I found mad. This was the palace of the famous Empress Cixi (The Dragon Lady), who was probably the most powerful woman in Chinese history. She earned the name Dragon Lady because she was very spiteful, cunning and manipulative (plus the likelihood of poisonings), however she also embraced change, and launched this ancient country from the last imperial empire into the modern age. She definitely had good taste, when you look at this place, as she was responsible for it's refurbishment and addition of many features. The ticketing here is done in two tiers - access to the lake/park, and the other access to inside the main palace. My advice is, if you have the time, buy both, and spend the whole day out at this amazing place.

The Summer Palace lies in the northwest of Beijing, between the 4th and 5th Ring Roads. Although it is called a palace in many languages, it is more accurately called a park; its Chinese name (頤和園 - Yíhéyuán) therefore means "Garden of Preserving Harmony." The immense park complex, covering an area of ​​2.9 km², consists of two main parts: Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake. Naturally, the majority of the 3,000 buildings are located on and around Longevity Hill. The very origins of the Summer Palace complex date back to 1153, when Wanyang Liang, ruler of the Jin Dynasty, moved his capital to Yanjing (present-day Beijing) and had a palace built near Jade Spring Hill. In 1271, the engineer Guo Shoujing commissioned the construction of waterworks, creating the Western Lake. In 1494, the Hongzhi Emperor commissioned a temple for his wet nurse on Longevity Hill, but it quickly fell into disrepair. His successor, the Zhengde Emperor, built a palace on the shores of Western Lake and transformed the surrounding area into an imperial garden. However, it was the rulers of the Qing Dynasty who were responsible for the Summer Palace's current appearance. In 1749, the Qianlong Emperor decided to build a palace for his mother near Longevity Hill and to expand Western Lake to improve Beijing's water supply. The earth excavated from Kunming Lake was used to enlarge Longevity Hill. The construction of the palace and the lake was completed in 1764 at a cost of over 4.8 million silver taels (equivalent to US$1.44 billion today). The design of the palace and garden is based on Chinese mythology and various beautiful locations in China. In 1860, during the Second Opium War, the Summer Palace was occupied and looted by British and French troops to pressure the Chinese government. The most famous name associated with the Summer Palace is that of Empress Dowager Cixi, the woman who was the unofficial ruler of China for 47 years. She enjoyed staying there, and between 1884 and 1895, she spent millions of taels earmarked for the modernization of the Chinese navy on the construction of palaces and the expansion of the complex. (The Stone Boat, incidentally, is said to be an ironic hint at the origin of the money.) In 1900, at the end of the Boxer Rebellion, the Summer Palace was again ransacked by Western troops, but two years later Cixi had the complex restored. After Puyi's abdication in 1912, the Summer Palace became the private property of the Qing family and opened to a paying public two years later. After the founding of the People's Republic of China, the palace was nationalized and renovated, and over time became one of Beijing's most popular tourist attractions. In 1988, the historical and cultural importance of the Summer Palace was confirmed when UNESCO designated it a World Heritage Site. The Summer Palace is an immense complex, with so much to see, so allow plenty of time—it's absolutely worth it!

Looming over Beijing on the north side of Kunming Lake, is the impressive royal summer palace. Calling it simply a palace is not really adequate, the surrounding area is all part of a large estate of parks, temples and other buildings. The architecture is pretty spectacular, vibrant coloured buildings, tree lined paths between little courtyards and elegantly decorated covered walkways barely scratches the surface. It's a long way up and having come through the north face I had no idea of the view over the lake that awaits. Beijing stretches far away to the south with little in the way of taller buildings to obstruct the view. Descending the south face stairs brings you to the lake itself, from here you can take a boat over to the south bank then walk over the famous Seventeen-Arch Bridge (Shiqikong Qiao). For a tourist there is simply not enough time in a day to view it all, as a local you'd spend a week here and still find some new corner you'd not found previously.

Well, well, well. This is probably the second-most overcrowded place in Beijing. Fortunately, this is a big area where people can spread easily. One of my favorite spots to visit in the Beijing area! Truly a historical gem. Amazing oasis right in the middle of a huge metropolis. Tons of walking but plenty of places to stop in the shade. Plenty of places to eat. There is so much to do here. It will take you many hours to see it. We got the cassette tour but did not find it very useful. The gift shops were small and cramped but had really great souvenirs. It is very crowded. The climb to the top of the stairs was brutal.

One of my favourite places to visit in Beijing 💖 If you plan on going, take note of: 1. Weather (we went during a heatwave, and it was HOT. Recommend going in the evening/cooler months - we went in Aug); 2. Summer holidays (it seems it’s the school holidays in Aug, and we were greeted by THRONGS of people. It was insane.)
Summer Palace is stunning! I wish I was there while it was in bloom. Hire a guide, its much more enjoyable. Make sure to see all the Budda sculptures and there are 888 Buddha's on the wall.

Given the name Summer Palace, it is not wrong to expect that this place would be ideal during the summer months. However, during my winter visit, I still don't think it is a place to be missed. The long walkway is still impressive, and the ancient Chinese architecture still breathtaking. In fact during our private guided tour (engaged from the official booth at the entrance), the guide even said during the summer months it gets so crowded, it is often difficult to even walk. We managed to walk stretches of the palatial grounds with very minimal human traffic, so I would say it, regardless of when you are keen to visit, please do so, as it is worth it.
A very elaborate and beautiful place. There is a lot to see and you can easily spend a day there. Might want to check the calendar and avoid visiting on a Chinese holiday as the crowds are huge.
Absolutely nice place to visit. But it's too cold in winter. Can consider other seasons of the year. Do look out for the historical parts and history.

Traditional tourist spot that's well kept and maintained. Recommended place to visit on a cool day otherwise bring umbrella to shield from the summer sun and bring lots of cold beverage. Did not see any nearby parking spot so just be prepared to walk. We were dropped off from our shuttle so did not have to walk far.

Wow. Just wow. Would highly recommend this place and to spend a few hours here, if not most of the day. It's an enormous park filled with temples, pavilions, theatres, bridges and walkways. Climbing up/down the hill takes you through vividly painted corridors to the main temple, where you will have excellent views of Kunming Lake. If you're travelling by metro (or by taxi for that matter), I recommend entering through the entrance nearest to Beigongmen stop, which is a 5 minute walk away. This will mean you're at the top of the hill and get to see the main Summer Palace, with the views overlooking the lake. You can then make your way down the hill (there are steps to walk down) towards the lake and walk around that area. There's entrances/exits dotted all over the place, but I'd recommend one on the Eastside as it is a 15 minute walk to the metro station Xiyuan, which will mean you don't need to walk back up the hill again. I only spent a couple of hours here as I was short of time, but wish I could have been here longer to soak up the atmosphere. Would highly recommend.
It's definitely worth 2 hours just to walk around this lake. Unfortunately you cannot enter the pagoda on top of the hill. 30 Yuan Entrance fee...

Beautiful place to visit but be prepared to deal with crowds any time you visit. We went in the rain and we still had more tour groups than we could count. That said, understanding that the Summer palace is situated on a man made lake from hundreds of years ago is mind boggling! The effort it took to excavate the lake in these pictures is astounding. The architecture... The stairs... The temples... The stairs... The park... Be prepared to walk A LOT! Absolutely beautiful...

Very beautiful ancient palace over 300 years old. Regardless of old sad stories, this place is worth visiting. The environment is so good and gave relaxing vibes. The lake was human made and it was so big.

A very beautiful palace that overlooks a beautiful lake from a high vantage hill. There is a very long covered walkway which is about 700m by the lake. This walkway has beautiful paintings and is a very scenic walk. There are many different buildings and temples that are very historic and beautiful. Do take note that these buildings are not next to the lake and you will need to take a look at a map to find and visit these buildings.

Summer Palace is huge so expect to wander all over the place. Definitely worth the visit! Prepare your passport and a form of payment such as AliPay or WeChat Pay. Short video to get an idea of what to expect starting at 0:05 - 2:13. https://youtu.be/hZ9MHLyjuoQ

The summer palace is so incredibly beautiful. I could walk around the ground for hours!! There is an incredible view every corner you turn. I could not stop taking pictures!! Definitely worth a visit!

This is one of the most beautiful pieces of traditional Chinese architecture I've had the pleasure of witnessing. The gardens are amazing and the roof details are all kinds of incredible. The colors will blow your mind and the beauty of the lake will take your breath away. I would highly recommend making this part of trip if headed to Beijing!

reviews.authorName: T R U N G H I Ế U (Life Is Too HarDDD)
reviews.text: Cool place to watch the sunset. Might be over crowded during the weekend. The toilets are not very clean. Still worth visiting when you come to Beijing
Beautiful views, and very rich in history. Definitely recommended to visit. It’s good to have guide as there is a lot of interesting information.

It’s amazing and mind blowing how excessive the life’s of the Royalty were in the past. Them aside, the people I am most impressed with are those to designed and built this place. This place is huge and the lake around it is amazingly. As you walk around the Palace look up there are equally as much beauty as you can see ahead. The details on the doors, the gate, the pathway, gazebos it’s truly astonishing. This place is so big, there was point during my visit where I was quite certain even the Emperor himself may not have been to every part of this palace in his lifetime. Another must visit destination when in Beijing

The boat ride on the lake was pleasant though, I’ll give them that. Would I recommend it? Sure, if you’re in Beijing anyway and have some time to kill. Just don’t expect to be overwhelmed by the size like everyone claims you will be. It’s tiny 2.9km2
Wonderful path leading to the palace where you can visit lots of interesting temples and gardens

Supremely beautiful place, basically a collection of palaces, lakes and parks. Bigger than the Forbidden Palace in size! It might take almost an entire day to explore the place completely. Highly accessible by metro and road, with very good connectivity. The tickets are fairly priced and one can choose the sections that one would want to visit if they are pressed for time, or take a combo ticket and explore the entire place if there is no time constraint. A must visit while in Beijing:)

Very beautiful place with plenty of sightseeing spots which you have to spend at least 3 hrs to go through. Don’t miss the Kunming Lake, Buddha hill, Suzhou street and the old house of former king. You will see very different scenarios here in different season. So, 1 visit is never enough.
For me, this is my favourite place in the whole China. It is outstanding and worth the trip t9 come t9 visit this place. The scenery is mind-blowing, peaceful, and tranquil.

This is one of the best tourist attractions in Beijing. If you are visiting, you must go. The views are breathtaking and there's a small hike up a mountain. The view is worth it. If you plan on going. Bring money for food because you are going to spent at least 3-5 hours here. Also bring water if you're visiting in the summer.
Beautiful place in Beijing. With a very interesting architecture and full f history and details the Summer Place is a magnificent place for a visit and a boat ride in its lake.

Lots to explore here. The buildings are kept in really good condition so you can experience the details and effort put into the exteriors of all the infrastructure. The interiors are not that impressive. Make sure to wear comfy shoes and appropriate clothing as you will do some hiking to get to the temple and the island areas and will be walking great distances. Allow yourself at least 3 hours to explore the grounds.
great place. theres a tall hill. also check out the island in the middle or the lake and go and see the museum. fun fact: the lake is entirely man made which means it was dug by hand

Wonderfull park. I rather prefer the Chinese style of non-symmetrical park which morphs well with Chinese bi-symmetrical architectural style. There's a lot of shade during the summer so it isn't too hot, out of all the parks I think it's the least hot. Be wary when you rent the boats, they only come back to where you started, it isn't the same company on different sides of the lake unfortunately so you can't shortcut that way.
Go early in the morning when the rising sun shows off the gardens and ponds in its full splendor. Words fail when you stand next to a living thriving tree planted 400 years ago...
Beautiful old palace that must seen if you visit Beijing, although the front is a lot of climbing but at the back there is a fantastic lakes with fabulous views.

We reached here around 4pm, and managed to avoid most of the huge tour groups. The weather wasn’t too hot too and it was a pleasure to walk around at our own pace with some private walking space. Many restrooms, souvenir shops and food available throughout the place and there are boat rides available if you’re not a fan of walking one round of the lake. The last entry to the summer palace is at 6pm, but you can stay inside until much later. Do note that if you’re keen to visit the other attractions/sites/boat rides within Summer Palace, most of them close around 5pm. The sunset here is really beautiful.

What a reverent and beautiful place. Plan a whole day and be sure to purchase admission into the summer palace itself and prepare to walk up a lot of stairs but the views are incredible and the crowd thins out a lot inside. We also visited Suzhou Street at the north entrance... what a sweet gem of a little village. So fun for our teen girls.

So beautiful, favorite place to visit again and again. I've been here all different seasons of the year. Five times over the course of the it 30 years and I just enjoy exploring different facets of the extensive grounds. They lake, the buildings, the plants, SuZhou street is my favorite. It closes at 4 though so don't wait too late. The marble boat is beautiful as well and the hike up to the Pagoda is with the view. As with most Chinese buildings at historic sites you don't actually get to go in, so you mostly admire the architecture. I was a bit sad that they don't care more for their ancient relics. The gifts to the emperor that your could kind of see behind the dirty glass hadn't been dusted for years. The park is really too big to see in one day so just choose an area to enjoy. It's worth paying for the up graded ticket as otherwise you need to pay again to go up to the Pagoda and SuZhou street. The boats weren't available in November.
Definitely a must see while in Beijing. The place though is not suitable for wheelchair access

Today is the first Chinese working day after 1st-5th May' vacation. From March 2024, I've travelled 3 times in Qingdao, Xiamen, Beijing about 10 days each. I'm so impressed Chinese government that love their people individually (valuable composition of the nation). They take care of cost of living, daily life security (I have seen old men with red flag at bus stops until 9:00 a.m. to help traffic, soldier, officers all around only whenever you need help.) and comfortability. The summer palace north gate (line4 beikongmenJan Exit C) is closed, so I must walk around to go in east gate, then pass this cultural hotel and get out at South gate(2.2km). In vast area of summer palace, you walk around with online chinese instrumental classical songs relaxation, good feeling. Outside south gate, old men are swimming and across the street is a swimming pool behind the mountain.

This place was amazing!! The prices are a bit on the expensive side but the experience of being there and seeing the beautiful landscape, structures and the temple makes it worthwhile. Soft comfortable walking shoes are a must!! Bring snacks and water as well. The restaurants inside are over priced.
Great architecture, easy to walk and not overcrowded (in the winter!). It is worth a visit when in Beijing

Summer Palace is a must-visit attraction in Beijing It is huge and made for the emperor of China It has a big lake at the centre. When you visit there at summer, it will be up to 40 Celsius at noon so bring more water or you can buy there. There are several places you can visit inside but most places are crowded

Don’t forget to walk along the long corridor, this man made lake and palace is incredible. It’s packed with tourists but where else not in this forbidden city. Some tourists just didn’t care you were taking a photo and they just walked pass the camera. However on the sunny day, the picturesque perfect worth the fuzziness and sweats.

Beautiful palace and lake. Make sure you climb up the stairs to the top of the palace to see the views of the lake at the top. Also walk all the way to the end of the water front to see the Ivory boat. Lots of crowds on weekends so go on a weekday.

When it Beijing, your visit is not complete without visiting the Summer Palace. The place is 290 hectares and almost 270 years in existence…we went there past 5pm and we need to get a bike inside before it gets dark…it is a good place for walking, jogging and biking…next time I will visit, I will make sure to be there earlier to see more of its surroundings and history
One of many beautiful places to visit in Beijing. Take your time at each one though because they all have something different to offer as well as many different stories to tell.

Well worth a visit I had a tour guide who explained the history which was very cheap and also made it a lot more easier to understand as there wasn't many signs. There is lots of walking so be careful in going at mid day as. Take plenty of drinks.

Enter from the N or East by taking subway. A couple of hours gives you enough time to take a quick walk. More time is nice and you can do about a 5-6 mile loop around the palace and temples. Lots of shady walks in this beautiful park. You can get out on the lake with boats though on the day we went everything was shut down. Apparently people don’t like to get out on the water during lightning storm. Go figure. If you get hungry you can get sausages or many other high calorie snacks. There does not seem to be a good restaurant though some places have tea. Hike to the pagoda and get a beautiful view of the city.
Beautiful and peaceful place with stunning gardens and lake views. A must-see in Beijing!

Walking around the Summer Palace can be tiring, but the landscape and the environment is well worthy. Climb the hill from North and walk down to the Kunming lake through the palace to feel the history surrounding you. Try to delete the crowd of tourists out of your eyes, and imagine being the emperor walking there on his own, while thinking of his duties towards the country. All that magnificent beauty was just built for you!

An experience of a lifetime. A day trip is not enough to appreciate the extent of this amazing historical place. The art and architecture flows into one another like it is inseparable. However, the sheer number of tourists can be overwhelming if it is your first time to Beijing.

Historical place whereby the Emperor used to go in summer time. There's a lot to see i.e. garden, lake, temple, long corridor, the architectural of the building, bridge, and etc. It is a huge place and a lot of walking. Prepare a walkable shoes. Theres boat outside of the temple which is kinda short cut to get u fast to the exit with a fee.

What a beautiful spot to start a visit to Beijing. On the recommendation of a friend, I was advised to buy my ticket in advance but it's not necessary for this time of year (paid double online for 50 yuan). None the less, you should be able to buy at the gate for 25 yuan. I started at the West Gates and made my way up to the Palace. Be prepared to put in the miles, but certainly worth it for views

Entry Ticket: 20 Yuan Date of Visit: 23 March 2019 Visited this place during my official visit to Beijing. This is very well connected to subway metro. This summer palace is a very big area and it would take a whole day to see all points and walk around. You can experience what it is like being a King of an empire, it's power, majesty and esteem. and There is a huge and prestine lake that can be seen after walking and crossing some distance after the entry. There is a very beautiful bridge across the this water reservoir. During spring time there trees blossomed with white flowers and whole of the place looks so devine. A huge Buddha temple/monatery is built in lake vicinity where u need to climb few steps and pay 10 Yuan separately for entry. This temple has a statue of Buddha having about 8 hands that looks like lord Vishnu, an Indian diety. This place has its own peace and calmness. There are people who fly beautiful kites in afternoon/evening time. This makes the place so happening for family, kids and individuals. This can be seen in the pictures attached. Overall a great place that must be seen of you are in Beijing.
Beautiful nice place to walk. Lots of stairs if you climb up to the buildings. Walk along the lake is neat.

This Summer Palace is one of the top visitors list in winter. Freezing cold and windy adds the mood for photography. A great historical site where most visitors never stop taking selfie and photographs. Get yourself a hot cup coffee and enjoy the magnificent views.
I would say it’s an amazing place, but the crowds were so bad that I couldn’t enjoy it much unfortunately.

Stunning place, even in winter and despite the bitterly cold weather. We had a guide, who really brought the palace's fascinating history to life, and I definitely recommend doing the same. Plus wear very very warm clothes in winter!!

Wonderful place. Great for a relaxing walk through century-old history. By far one of the "must see" places in Beijing. They have student discounts on the entrance fees and they also offer audio guides in many languages.
A little crowded but totally worth the experience. Spend several hours there enjoying the gardens and definitely pay the extra buck to go up into the temple!
Interesting landmark from Chinese history. Worth visiting if you like to walk while observing a good preserved place. Great view of the temple from the bottom, and watch the boats at the lake.

Despite the name, it’s beautiful year round! We visited in January and they had some fun winter activities too. We rode ski sleds on the frozen lake and enjoyed touring the whole area. It’s ornate and beautiful!

It's called a Summer Palace in English, and I went in the Winter, so maybe that's why it wasn't as beautiful as I expected to be. It was a windy, cold day, and trying to walk around this massive garden was long and tiring. I would come here when it's warmer, so I can enjoy more and longer (going on boat rides, and such). However, the palace that was at the north center of the entire garden was amazingly beautiful, and the view looking down the entire lake in front was phenomenal. The # of steps to walk up is quite steep and long, but it's totally worth it. It just amuses me when I think about how much effort was taken to build this on a steep mountain side. It cost extra 10 rmb to get into the center palace, and it closes earlier than the rest of the Summer Palace.

Walked around the lake. About 8 km so plan enough time. But worth every step! Beautiful trees just starting to bloom. Fragrant peach trees, weeping willows, magnolia and many more. Loved every second.

The main attractions of this place are Longevity hill and Kunming Lake. The palace is very vast and it will take lot of time if you plan to walk around. We entered the palace after saying goodbye to Jenny and the driver through the east gate and it’s more suitable for us to get out from the north gate as the Subway station is near to it. We paid an all inclusive entrance ticket of RMB 60/- per head, however there are tickets available for each place separately. We started walking seeing the sites we could see along our way after walking for few minutes we could see the giant lake in front of us. We saw the arch bridge at a distance and started walking towards it along the side of the lake were we saw people relaxing and enjoying the view of this beautiful scenery sitting in the chairs in the shades of tree along the shores of the lake. We opted for the boat service from the center of the lake to the other side towards the North for which we paid extra of RMB 15/- per head as the boat rides are not included in the tickets.

Built around 1750, the Summer Palace is located in the Haidian District northwest of Beijing, 15 kilometers (9 miles) from the downtown area. As the largest and most well-preserved royal park in China, 'The Museum of Royal Gardens' includes Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake, and over 3,000 man-made ancient structures, including pavilions, towers, bridges, corridors with gardens. One should consider spending at least a half day to explore, with winter activities including skating, manual and motorized sleds.

I have been to Summer Palace at least over a dozen times, perhaps over two dozens of times as I lost count. I had many very nice photos, unfortunately, I was not able to upload to Google Maps for some unknown reason. I will try to use my laptop to upload those photos if possible. stay tuned. Thanks!

Absolutely amazing! A most see if you're going to Beijing! It was my favorite place of everything I saw! It's better to go early in the morning before 11 am or after 3pm because it gets crowded even during week days. It gets around 3 hours to enter and to see everything...

Again a must visit place if you are in beijing. It is better to buy a combined pass rather than individual passes. Also, if you are a student don't forget to carry your ID card as you spoiled get tickets at half the price for the same. Do wear hoped sports shoes as it requires some amount of walking and climbing. There a is a lot of history around it, please do take a guide if you read it. There are other places near the summer palace so keep some time handy for them. As the name suggest do not visit it in summer, it is gonna be hot and might not envoy the visit. Please enjoy the photos I have attached. If u find my post helpful, do like them.

I think I went during the peak season of visiting and hence all the crowd. A beautiful historic place with information in chinese, Japanese, Korean, English and French. Most halls are now redecorated as exhibitions and sales. Gardens and lake are beautiful.

There are two gardens like this in Beijing, and I choose this one only because it is more famous around the locals and the tourists. This garden is extremely huge that I can’t go through all of the sites, so I row the boat. Rowing the boat is fastest way to go through most of the sites, seeing them from distance.

Very pretty place, but unfortunately I was here during Chinese Labour day, so the place was absolutely packed with people. And a pickpocket stole my all-inclusive ticket to the different attractions. I mostly just stayed ontop of the mountain to avoid the crowds. But I'd still recommend people going here, it's all very beautiful, just make sure you're not going during any busy holidays. And don't keep your tickets in your backpocket, I was aware that putting stuff in back pocket was risky, but I thought "who would steal a ticket?" and they certainly showed me.

The Summer Palace is a beautiful historical place to visit. We spent a couple of hours here and would recommend 2-3 hours to visit. Temperatures were hot the first week of June: about 38-41 C! Nice thing though is that there is quite a bit of shade amongst the trees and a light breeze from the huge lake. Crowds were not bad at all on a weekday afternoon. Our Tour Guide also informed us that it has the longest corridor in the world; it's very picturesque with the paintings/pictures/murals. And there's a couple of months during the summertime that the lotus flowers will bloom in the lake!

Majestic palace with many interesting palaces and buildings. But the most interesting is the lake, very large for a man made lake, built to resemble the west lake in Hangzhou. Recommended for instagram lovers.

The New Summer palace, now UNESCO world heritage, after being various times destroyed by french british troops in the past colonial areas, is the essence of Chinese palace and temple architecture. Huge gates, hundreds of pavilions, parks bridges. Take a full day, stroll around the lake shore, take a boat and be not surprised that you are not the only one enjoying this wonderful magical place.

Summer Palace is the biggest Royal Garden in the vicinity of Beijing City. Need to purchase a ticket to enter the Summer Palace. Usually bit crowded on weekends. Good for families and kids. Summer Palace is a place that showcase the Chinese History. Beijing subway is the easiest way to reach this place. On subway line 4 to Beigongmen and then take the Exit D. Then walk to the west for about 5 minutes that would bring you to the North Entrance of the Summer Palace. There are many tourist attractions inside Summer Palace.

Amazing!! A must see, makesure you come early the queues are crazy! It's busy mostly with local tourists. If you are a student, bring your student card, you get a discount. Similarly with those who are retired. Wear comfortable shoes. You can easily spend half a day here. It may be worth bringing some snacks, as not all the restaurants were open. PS it's worth getting the whole package (rather than just the entrance fee)

Another place that shall not be missed when visiting Beijing. This place is huge, larger than Forbidden City. Buy the through ticket @ RMB 60 if you want to explore all the sites. Make sure not to miss the Marble Boat, Tower of Buddhist Incense, Kunming Lake, Seventeen Arch Bridge, Hall of Benevolence and Longevity. Nanhu island can also be a another spot to see by taking a boat ride.

No regrets, the one hour travel from the city is worth it. Absolutely beautiful, stunning, amazing Chinese architecture! I entered from the north gates, and the ferry service was not operating so did alot of walking, but it was all worth it.
The layout of the palace, the architecture, the history, and more all combine to make it an unforgettable location for anyone visiting Beijing — or China for that matter!

My favorite spot in Beijing. I spent almost 7 hours to hanging around in this place. I buy a full ticket for 60 yuan (12 USD) so I have access to all gate. But you could buy just the entrance fee then decided later which one to visit. If you want to buy souvenir, I recommend to buy it in sunzhou street. It cheaper than in the gift shop inside. Bring comfortable shoe because each attraction are far away.
Beautiful place. A must visit for Beijing. Be prepared to walk a lot though, and be prepared to see a huge number of people. Also, it's freezing cold in the winter...

The Summer Palace and its surrounding imperial garden with surrounding natural landscape is a classic example of Chinese Imperial dwelling. The area is dotted with not only Summer Palace but other spot of tourist intetest like Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake, consiting of hundreds of scenic spots, more than 20 courtyards and thousands of ancient structures, and hundreds years old trees. It will require at least a couple of days to tour the entire area spanning several square kilometres The noted scenins spots are the Long Gallery, Tower of Buddhist Incense, Suzhou Market Street, Marble Boat, Garden of Harmonious Interests, Seventeen Arch Bridge, and Ancient Stage The park consists of three main areas - The Hall of Benevolent Longevity, which was once the place for taking care of internal affairs, and diplomatic and political activities by Emperor Guangxu and Empress Cixi. The next is Hall of Joy and the Hall of Jade Billows which was used as the living area for Emperor Guangxu and Empress Cixi The last viewing area of the Summer Palace is around Long Gallery and Back Hill. This was used for recreation and luxurious living of the emperor and the empress. There are threee buildings on the southern slope of Longevity Hill - The Hall of Dispelling Clouds, Tower of Buddhist Incense, and the Hall of the Sea of Wisdom. The magnificent bridge on Kumming Lake with Seventeen Arches helping you to cross the Kumming Lake. On the banks of Kunming Lake one can also spot the famous sites of Marble Boat, Bronze Ox, and Spring Pavilion. Suzhou Market Street, is hundreds of year old and even today bustling with stores The Summe Palace is a must visit tourist spot around Beijing

Don't take a taxi to the 'old summer palace', it's a park! You have to pay by cash, they don't take WePay. The gardens and lakes are well maintained and clean. Take a ride in the boats near the lake. The temples and forest are at the top of the hill and the real highlight. The scenery is spectacular, especially in summer when you hear the birds and insects chirping.

I don't know what to say..having heard about it as a must do when in Beijing ,I was kind of not too impressed. Yes it is a massive place but cannot associate it with the opulence seen in even small palaces of princely states in India. There is a sense of space ,it is quite sprawled out with its own lake and the long corridor beside the lake and a Buddhist temple on the hill top adjacent to it,must have been quite a serene , relaxing and romantic place for the emperor,the empress but doesn't seem that way with the huge crowd milling around.
One of the most beautiful places to visit! Although there are a lot of people, you can always find somewhere quiet to have a break and enjoy the scenery

It is a huge and beautiful place to see, worth the money. Although you need to come early in the morning if you want to see the whole park, because some of the places close at 4pm and the park itself at 5pm. Pd: you can get lost easily at the mountain paths.

The Summer Palace is a combination gardens, lakes, and palaces. It covers 2,9 square kilometres, very large and very crowded. Many tourists from around the world come here. It was an imperial garden in Qing Dynasty. If you come here in summer, the weather is very hot. You need half of the day to see everything. Many spots to take pictures here.

One of the best historical places in Beijing. Even in 36C I could enjoy excellent architecture, views on the lake,and especially the hilly landscape. It's much different from (for me a bit boring) Forbidden city or Temple of Heaven. Forests,stones,hidden buildings and towers-excellent.

If you are going in the summer try to get there shortly before the tickets stop being sold at 6 pm, and consider entering via the North Gate (near the Beigongmen subway station). The park remains open until 8, and the crowds will be much smaller and its a nice walk from the North Gate to the main (East) gate (which is about a 10 minute walk from the Xiyuan subway station).
Beautiful, very cooling in summer. Nice to sit down, draw with gentle wind and manmade lake. You can ride a boat. Afternoon or morning walk around the summer palace.

Definitely need to go there if you come to Beijing. Only 50 rmb for the ticket, which include all the entrances in the palace, during low season. I spent 3 hrs in here but only visited half of the palace( I took lots of photos). You may need 5 to 6 hrs for the whole palace. There are several spots you have to visit, the bridge, the lake and the highest tower. Reminder: bring you own food as the food inside the garden is so expensive. And find a day that is not misty.

This place is little bit far from center of Beijing but the long journey will reward you. This palace is very huge and beautiful. If you can visit this place in the early morning, I highlu recommend you to go there.
One of the most famous attractions in China. Very crowded during summer vacations. Better being here during weekdays. A royal garden full of buildings and arts, which are rich in connotations.
The place is so big that you need your half day exploring it, boats are the main transport here to get you around that cost me 30RMB each ride and it's too crowded in the main building too.

Summer Palace is a great place to visit, there are this big lake in the middle. Reccomended for historical lovers. Bench and Trash can are available around the Park. However, during winter, beware of slipping because of snow. It was so slippery, that I almost fell.

This is my first time to go abroad.I went to Beijing five days to take part in a contest.During the trip to Beijing,my mother and I visited Beijing Summer Palace for a walk.That was the first time that I really feel relaxed and happy.And the view was very beautiful.I think everything is worth it. I was able to travel to Beijing through this competition, and this trip really opened my eyes.If you went to Beijing,I really recommend you to visit Beijing Summer Palace.That really broadened my horizons.What a marvelous sight it is!
Huge and quiet place where you can easily spend and entire day. The scenery is really nice and there is a lot to see. It’s also good if you want to take a walk or exercise

Summer palace, not very well maintained as compare to my visit in 2015. All the building, walkway's painting is not well kept and very few tourists. Drink store owner told us that they will be moving out soon because business are just too poor. Most of the stores closed down due to poor management of the park. If you really must visit, would suggest you study the location map first because you don't want to waste your time and strength by just exploring the whole park, really there is nothing much to see now. You should just visit the Buddha temple (Wisdom Ocean) then take the short cut (on the left) to the tower to see the lake from high above. The Summer Palace, a UNESCO site, is a large area around and including Kunming Lake, consisting of a variety of cool sights like the Garden of Virtue and Harmony, the Hall of Dispelling Clouds, Suzhou Street, and of course the iconic Tower of Buddhist Incense that stands out on the hill above Kunming Lake. This is where the Empress Dowager Cixi and other Chinese Royalty spent time during the summer away from the sometimes stifling Beijing heat, and it in addition to being noticeably cooler (and downright frigid during winter), it is full of natural and architectural beauty. Do yourself a favor and buy the combination ticket, because the must-see sites are not included in the basic cost of admission, and a visit to the Summer Palace wouldn't be complete without them. An absolute must-visit attraction if you find yourself in Beijing

The Summer Palace, in Chinese Yihe Yuan, is now the largest and the most well-preserved imperial garden in China, counted as one of the four famous Chinese imperial gardens (the other three being Chengde Summer Palace, Suzhou Humble Administrator's Garden, and Suzhou Lingering Garden). It was listed as World Heritage by UNESCO in 1998. Situated in Haidian District, 15km from downtown Beijing, the Summer Palace occupies an area of 290 hectares, with the lake taking up three quarters of its total area. It is designed around Kunming Lake and Longevity Hill as the key features, modeled on West Lake in Hangzhou, and draws from design techniques and artistic conception of gardens from the south of China. This large landscaped and well-preserved garden is known as the Chinese imperial garden museum. The Summer Palace was created in 1750, originally as the Emperor’s garden retreat in the Qing Dynasty. It was called Qingyi Garden at first. The major project in its creation was the Three Hills and Five Gardens. The Three Hills refers to Longevity Hill, Fragrant Hill, and Jade Spring Hill, and the Five Gardens are Jingyi Garden, Jingming Garden, Qingyi Garden, and the surrounding Changchun Garden and Yuanming Yuan). Qingyi Garden was destroyed by British and French troops during the Second Opium War in the 1860s. In 1888 Empress Cixi spent a large amount of money to rebuild a similar garden, for luxury and pleasure in summer time, called the Summer Palace. In the late Qing Dynasty, 1900, the Summer Palace was damaged again by eight European countries’ allied forces, and many national treasures were looted. The palace was repaired in 1903. Later in the period of Kuomintang in the power of regime, the Summer Palace was damaged again. After 1949, the Summer Palace was repaired and protected by the Communist government, and on March 4, 1961, the Summer Palace was announced as the first National Cultural Relics Protection Site. The Summer Palace has a great combination of imperial garden features, immersed in the surrounding natural landscape. It reflects the imperial garden principle of "built by man with resources from nature". Summer PalaceApart from Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake, there are over a hundred scenic spots, more than 20 courtyards and 3,000 ancient structures, and 1,600 trees over a hundred years old. The Tower of Buddhist Incense, Long Gallery, Marble Boat, Suzhou Market Street, Seventeen Arch Bridge, Garden of Harmonious Interests, and Ancient Stage are the most noted scenic spots. The main viewing areas in the park are broadly divided into three sections. The first one is by the Hall of Benevolent Longevity, which was once the place for taking care of internal affairs, and diplomatic and political activities by Emperor Guangxu and Empress Cixi. The second sightseeing area is between the Hall of Joy and the Hall of Jade Billows. The courtyards were used as the living area for Empress Cixi and Emperor Guangxu with his concubines. Summer PalaceThe last viewing area is around Long Gallery and Back Hill. This area was for the imperial family's daily luxury and recreation. On the central axis of the south slope of Longevity Hill are located three magnificent buildings: Tower of Buddhist Incense, the Hall of Dispelling Clouds, and the Hall of the Sea of Wisdom. Tower of Buddhist Incense has three stories and eight sides. It is built on the slope of Longevity Hill and faces Kunming Lake, commanding a view of the whole park. The magnificent Seventeen Arch Bridge, poised above the vastness of Kunming Lake, is at its best when viewed reflecting on the water. On the shore of Kunming Lake are the famous sites of Marble Boat, Bronze Ox, and Spring Pavilion. Suzhou Market Street, adjacent to Front Lake, has various stores in the style of the bustle trading streets hundreds of years ago. The Summer Palace, along with the Forbidden City, and the Temple of Heaven, is a must-see imperial attraction of Beijing.
